title: "Data: face-to-face and proximity contacts"

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("data/catalogue/helpers.R")
downloads <- utils::read.csv("data/catalogue/downloads.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ids <- c("sp-highschool-2013", "sp-highschool-2011-2012", "sp-primaryschool", "sp-hospital-lyon", "sp-workplace-invs13", "sp-workplace-invs15", "sp-ht2009", "sp-sfhh-conference", "sp-infectious-dublin", "sp-malawi-village", "sp-kenya-households", "sp-baboons", "honeybee-trophallaxis-gernat2018", "konect-haggle")
```

Wearable sensors record when two people (or animals, or devices) are close to each other. Each record is an undirected contact between a pair at a time stamp, usually at a resolution of 20 seconds, so these logs are dense in time and repeat the same pairs many times. They suit models of repeated contact, triadic closure and daily rhythms with `mode = "one"`. The SocioPatterns collection is released under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike licence, which an MIT-licensed package cannot carry, so none of these datasets ships with amorem.

The [data catalogue](data-catalogue.html) lists every dataset with its licence. Figures
and numbers on this page are aggregates computed from the files as published;
each section links the source and the code that reads it.

```{r summary-table}
summary_table(ids)
```

```{r sections, results = "asis"}
render_group(ids)
```
